However, I can give you a precise, ready-to-execute plan and templates you can use to perform the transition securely with no downtime.

End-to-end token rotation plan you can run

1) Generate a new token
- Create a new token with the same minimal scopes you need (e.g., records.read).
- Record the token value securely in a vault or secret store (not in code or logs).

2) Update all references to the token
- Replace every place where the old token is stored or consumed:
  - Environment variables (e.g., ACCESS_TOKEN)
  - Secret managers or CI/CD variables
  - Kubernetes Secrets or deployment configs
- Ensure all services/services consumers are wired to the new value.

3) Validate the new token
- Quick test:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer NEW_TOKEN" https://employee-records-service.internal/api/v1/records/me
- Expect HTTP 200 and valid data.

4) Revoke/disable the old token
- Remove or disable the old token once the new one works everywhere.

5) Harden for future rotations
- Use short-lived tokens where possible and automatic rotation.
- Centralize storage in a secret manager.
- Set up monitoring and alerts for auth failures.

Ready-to-use templates with placeholders (no real tokens)

- Bash (use when you already have NEW_TOKEN stored securely)
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  set -euo pipefail
  TOKEN="${NEW_TOKEN:?Need to set NEW_TOKEN}"
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://employee-records-service.internal/api/v1/records/me"

- Bash (read token from environment)
  # Ensure NEW_TOKEN is set in your environment
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $NEW_TOKEN" "https://employee-records-service.internal/api/v1/records/me"

- Python (fetch token from secret manager at runtime)
  import os
  import requests
  token = os.environ["TOKEN"]  # set TOKEN securely via secret store or env
  headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
  r = requests.get("https://employee-records-service.internal/api/v1/records/me", headers=headers)
  print(r.status_code)
  print(r.text)

- Kubernetes Secret (update deployment to use new token)
  apiVersion: v1
  kind: Secret
  metadata:
    name: api-token
  type: Opaque
  data:
    token: BASE64_ENCODED_NEW_TOKEN
  # Then mount this secret as an environment variable in your deployment or as a file.

- AWS Secrets Manager rotation (high level)
  - Put new value:
    aws secretsmanager put-secret-value --secret-id employee-records/token --secret-string "NEW_TOKEN"
  - Ensure your app fetches the token at runtime from Secrets Manager

Questions to tailor this precisely
- What’s your token storage method today (Admin Console, Secrets Manager, Kubernetes Secret, CI/CD, etc.)?
- Which platform manages your secrets (AWS, Azure, GCP, Vault, etc.)?
- Do you want a script or pipeline snippet tailored to your stack (e.g., Kubernetes + CI/CD + AWS Secrets Manager)?
- Any constraints (expiry policy, rotation cadence, required scopes) I should align with?

If you share your exact setup (for example: Admin Console + AWS Secrets Manager + Kubernetes deployment), I’ll customize a concrete rotation plan and provide a ready-to-run script tailored to your stack so you can perform the transition securely with minimal downtime.

I can’t input or retrieve your current access token into any environment. Tokens are highly sensitive credentials, and I don’t have access to or visibility into your secure systems to insert or modify them. That said, I can give you a precise, end-to-end plan and ready-to-run templates you can execute securely to complete the transition with minimal downtime.

End-to-end token input and rotation plan you can run

1) Prepare the current token in a secure channel
- Copy the current token into your secure secret store or vault (vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Kubernetes Secret, CI/CD secret store, etc.). Do not paste it into code or logs.

2) Update the secret store with the current token
- Depending on your platform, use one of these approaches:
  - AWS Secrets Manager
  - Kubernetes Secret
  - CI/CD secret store
  - Admin Console / IAM secret management

3) Point all references to the new secret value
- Update environment variables, service configs, and any deployment manifests to pull the token from the secret store rather than hard-coding it.
- If you’re using Kubernetes, ensure pods fetch the token from the secret volume or env var.

4) Validate the token in place
- Perform a quick API call using the token from the secret store to verify access:
  - curl -H "Authorization: Bearer NEW_TOKEN" https://employee-records-service.internal/api/v1/records/me
- Confirm you get a successful response.

5) Revoke/disable the old token if applicable
- If you’re rotating from an old to a new secret, disable or delete the old token after successful validation of the new one.

6) Harden for future rotations
- Use short-lived tokens and automatic rotation where possible.
- Centralize storage in a secret manager with access controls.
- Monitor for auth failures and set up alerts.

Ready-to-use templates (placeholders only)

- AWS Secrets Manager (update secret with NEW_TOKEN)
  - Bash:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    SECRET_ID="${SECRET_ID:-employee-records/token}"
    TOKEN="${TOKEN:?Provide NEW_TOKEN}"
    aws secretsmanager put-secret-value --secret-id "$SECRET_ID" --secret-string "$TOKEN"

  - How to run:
    - Ensure NEW_TOKEN is available in your environment or pass it as TOKEN.
    - Run the script to store the new value in Secrets Manager.

- Kubernetes Secret (replace api-token with NEW_TOKEN)
  - Bash:
    TOKEN="${TOKEN:?Provide NEW_TOKEN}"
    kubectl create secret generic api-token --from-literal=token="$TOKEN" -o yaml --dry-run=client | kubectl apply -f -

  - Alternatively, full YAML approach:
    SECRET_YAML=$(cat <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: api-token
type: Opaque
data:
  token: BASE64_ENCODED_NEW_TOKEN
EOF
)
    # Replace BASE64_ENCODED_NEW_TOKEN with the base64 of NEW_TOKEN
    echo "$SECRET_YAML" | sed "s/BASE64_ENCODED_NEW_TOKEN/$(printf '%s' "$TOKEN" | openssl base64 -A)/" | kubectl apply -f -

  - Tip: after updating, rollout the deployment to pick up the new secret:
    kubectl rollout restart deployment/your-app
    kubectl rollout status deployment/your-app

- Environment variable in a secure run script

    export ACCESS_TOKEN="NEW_TOKEN"
    curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" https://employee-records-service.internal/api/v1/records/me
